findings.exact_claim: The five parenthesized tensor products are vertices of the associator pentagon; the arrows are the two routes in the pentagon identity and the equation is A_3 A_2 A_1 = A_5 A_4.
findings.finding: The frozen HTML and original-resolution tiles show a red “diagram failed to render” panel with the raw tikzcd source instead of the pentagon. The adjacent prose and proof specify the intended five parenthesizations and route products, but the visual diagram is absent. Receipt sidecar reports one tikzcd diagram failure and zero KaTeX errors.
findings.suggested_repair: Repair the tikzcd source or adapt it to syntax accepted by the frozen local renderer, then recapture and verify all five parenthesized objects and the five associator arrows against the Statement and proof. The required composites are the three-arrow route A_3 A_2 A_1 and the two-arrow route A_5 A_4.

diagram_candidates.exact_source_claim: The square grid has vertices (i,j), physical qubits on edges outside the rough boundary set R, X-check incidence map ∂1:Q1→Q0, face-boundary map ∂2:Q2→Q1 with edges in R deleted, H_X=∂1 and H_Z=∂2^T; ∂1∂2=0, and left/right are rough while top/bottom are complementary dual boundaries.
diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: Labeled square-lattice surface-code cellulation with primal/dual boundaries and check supports
diagram_candidates.reason: The definition is geometric and fixes nonstandard boundary conventions that determine which edges are physical, which vertices index X checks, and how truncated face boundaries index Z checks. A small labeled cellulation makes these incidence maps and boundary deletions directly auditable; it adds useful geometric context to an otherwise abstract matrix description.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: For a generic d×d square-face patch, label the left and right vertical boundary edges R and distinguish those removed edges from physical data edges. Mark vertices outside R as X-check locations and square faces as Z-check locations. Draw one representative X support as the incident physical edges at a nonrough vertex and one representative Z support as the face boundary with any R edge omitted. Label the primal and dual boundary pairs and state the chain relation ∂1∂2=0. Verify the qubit count 2d² and exact index conventions against lines 36–56.
diagram_candidates.suggested_repair: An independent reviewer may decide whether a labeled cellulation figure is useful; if added, check the left/right rough-edge deletion, physical-edge count, X/Z supports, and chain-map relation against the frozen definition.

existing_diagram_checks.result: The only existing content diagram is the tikzcd pentagon in thm-qc-tqc-pentagon-coordinates. Its source and stated maps were checked against the adjacent statement and proof, but the local renderer replaced it with a failure panel, so its displayed arrow geometry and labels could not be visually checked. Every other assigned receipt reports tikz_count=0 and no diagram failures.

reviewed_observations.receipt_summary: All 56 receipt sidecars report no KaTeX errors; 0 item(s) report tikz_count>0 and 1 report diagram failure(s). Frozen snapshot and HTML hashes match assignment 07 for all items, and all 83 PNG hashes and dimensions match their receipts.
reviewed_observations.visual_summary: One confirmed rendering failure is reported for the missing pentagon diagram. No other confirmed LaTeX/KaTeX defect, overlap, or diagram-mathematics error was found in the individually viewed tiles. Long formulas and proof text remain legible in the captured continuation tiles; this report makes no numeric DOM overflow assertion.

limitations: Review covers only the 56 assigned frozen items and their local snapshots, HTML previews, receipts, and 83 captured tiles. No HTTP(S), live site, production route, or other lane was inspected.

This is a visual and diagram-rendering review, not a full mathematical proof audit. The failed pentagon could not be checked as a rendered figure; its intended maps were compared with the adjacent frozen Statement and proof.
No source item, status, publication state, application/tool file, or library content was modified.
